clue.text: Contrary to accepted beliefs it can be time-saving

definitions.note: the phrase describes an attitude of habitual denial and scepticism, standing for the noun naming that attitude

indicators.note: the clue says the letters of the following word can be turned into something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A claim that some heretical view might actually save people time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it can be' asks you to rearrange the letters of TIME-SAVING.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a habitual stance of denying or rejecting received opinions and doctrines.

clue.text: Talent denied to America?

parts.note: a refusal or denial is a flat no
US is the usual abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A complaint that some gift or ability is withheld from Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'denied to America' as a refusal said to the US. NOUS is British slang for common sense or practical wit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal British English for practical intelligence or shrewdness, a kind of native ability.

clue.text: What we suffer in turns

parts.note: read 'in turns' not as taking turns but as spinning round, which leaves anyone dizzy

explanation.surface: A grumble about hardships everyone endures one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning round produces dizziness, a reeling sensation in the head.

clue.text: Trunk with tangled roots

indicators.note: tangled roots are twisted out of order, so the word roots is rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree trunk with its roots twisted together.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of a body is the main part without head or limbs, a synonym.

clue.text: Trace of garment that is seen around the Greek capital

parts.note: a vest is an undergarment

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes round the next letter, so it encloses it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

indicators.note: the capital or head of a word is its first letter, here of Greek

explanation.surface: A remnant of some clothing spotted near Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' is a link word. 'the Greek capital' looks like Athens, but it is only the letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a small surviving sign or remnant of something, much as a trace is.

clue.text: Hang it, otherwise we pay out

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters of the two pieces are shuffled

parts.note: we, as an object, is us
to pay out money is to spend it

explanation.surface: An exasperated 'Hang it!' from someone faced with paying up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a link word. The letters of US and SPEND are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to hang it from above, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Puffed out bird

definitions.meaning: something smoked in a pipe, as a coarse cut of tobacco is
a cormorant-like seabird of British coasts

explanation.surface: A bird with its feathers fluffed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puffed out' looks like a description of the bird; it is tobacco that a smoker puffs out.
explanation.definitionFit: Shag is both a strong coarse tobacco smoked in pipes and a crested seabird related to the cormorant.

clue.text: Successors to "The Sound of Music"?

indicators.note: this asks for what something sounds like, so a word spoken is matched by another spelling

parts.note: airs are tunes or melodies, so music

explanation.surface: A question about who might follow the famous musical film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sound of Music' is the film title, but here it means the sound of AIRS. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirs are those who inherit and follow on after someone, i.e. successors.

clue.text: Left the country without restraint?

parts.note: literally, someone who quit the countryside headed for the city; idiomatically, someone who acted lavishly and with abandon

explanation.surface: Someone who fled abroad without being stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left the country' suggests emigrating, but it means leaving rural parts for town.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting with great enthusiasm or extravagance, and literally describes a trip from the countryside.

clue.text: One real tug can make it binding

indicators.note: the letters can be made into the answer, signalling a rearrangement of the pieces

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A sharp pull on something will make it tie fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligature is a cord or thread used for tying, so a binding.

clue.text: Believed guilty, unlike Caesar's wife

definitions.meaning: the proverb says Caesar's wife must be above reproach and doubt

explanation.surface: Someone thought to have done wrong, in contrast to the proverbially blameless spouse of Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'Caesar's wife must be above suspicion' is the key: its opposite position is beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Being suspected means people think you guilty; the proverb sets Caesar's wife above any such doubt.

clue.text: See 10
It's deadly being moved into pleasant surroundings

indicators.note: pleasant surroundings means the synonym for pleasant goes around the other piece

parts.note: pleasant means nice

indicators.note: the letters of the word into are moved about, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Something lethal transferred into an agreeable setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a link word but it is fodder: rearranged as OTIN it goes inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: This alkaloid in tobacco is a poison, lethal in sufficient doses.

clue.text: An appurtenance a Hardy heroine recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy heroine remembered as an accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy was an English novelist; his best-known heroine is Tess.
explanation.definitionFit: An appurtenance is something belonging to or going with a property, a possession of value.

clue.text: Created havoc, as the Hindu deity said

parts.note: a deva is a god or divine being in Hinduism
said means stated

explanation.surface: A Hindu god is reported to have wrought destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Devastated in the active sense means laid waste or wrecked, causing havoc.

clue.text: Dish of green peas as an exception

indicators.note: the word as is excepted, taken out of the letters of green peas, and the rest rearranged

explanation.surface: A dish of peas, unusually.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of GREEN PEAS without A and S rearrange to give the answer; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece holding fruit or flowers, a serving dish.

clue.text: Punishment one may have a hand in

definitions.meaning: running the ... was a punishment between lines of men striking the victim

definitions.text: one may have a hand in
definitions.meaning: a protective glove that a hand fits inside

explanation.surface: A penalty in which one plays a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have a hand in' suggests taking part, but literally it means wearing it on your hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the old military punishment and a heavy armoured glove.

clue.text: TT wear

definitions.meaning: a pair of identical letters side by side
a close-fitting jacket worn by men in the past

explanation.surface: Clothing for the Isle of Man TT motorcycle races.
explanation.walkthrough: TT suggests the Isle of Man motorbike races, but here it is just two identical letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a pair of matching things and also a Renaissance man's jacket.

clue.text: Schooner of wine at Rotterdam, say

definitions.meaning: a schooner is a large glass, here filled with the fortified Portuguese wine
Rotterdam is a major Dutch harbour city

explanation.surface: A glass of wine drunk in the Dutch city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Schooner' tempts you towards ships at a harbour; it is a big glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A big glass of fortified wine, and also a description of a major harbour city.

clue.text: Attack on a sailor, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks a sound-alike: the spoken words match another spelling

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, so a sailor is a salt

explanation.surface: Reports of someone setting upon a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent attack, a synonym.

clue.text: Cry from worker on the square to a hanger-on

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so T
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker
ivy clings to walls and trees, hanging on

explanation.surface: A call from a labourer in the town square to a sycophant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from', 'on' and 'to' are link words. 'Hanger-on' suggests a sycophant but means the clinging plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantivy is an old hunting cry, a shout urging a galloping chase.

clue.text: Overlooking arched feature

parts.note: a curved line of hair on the face that sits above, and so overlooks, the eye

explanation.surface: An architectural arch that commands a view.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like architecture, but the arch is on a face.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the arch of hair on the ridge above each eye.

clue.text: Girl's name he spelt wrongly

indicators.note: spelt wrongly means the letters are put in the wrong order, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has misspelt a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Elspeth is a Scottish female first name, a form of Elizabeth.

clue.text: Implied when I indulge in finesse

indicators.note: the letter I indulges in, i.e. gets into, the synonym for finesse

parts.note: finesse in dealing with people is tact

explanation.surface: An implication when someone treats themselves to subtlety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being stated, so implied.

clue.text: Roman patrician not good of hearing

indicators.note: of hearing points to how the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a wrongdoer, someone not good, is a sinner

explanation.surface: A Roman noble said to be hard of hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike. Cinna was a Roman patrician family name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucius Cornelius Cinna was a Roman consul from a patrician family.

clue.text: Known to many, being of so recent development

indicators.note: a development is a change into a new form, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: Common knowledge because it happened lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is known to many people, it is no longer hidden or private.

clue.text: Where a number can circulate in Eire

definitions.text: Where a number can circulate in Eire

indicators.note: circulate means go around, so the word can goes around the other pieces

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number

explanation.surface: A question of where a figure can be passed around in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVAN is a county in the Republic of Ireland; 'in Eire' completes the whole-clue definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavan is an Irish county and town, a place in the Republic.

clue.text: Gritty associate of Chopin, by George!

definitions.text: Gritty associate of Chopin, by George!

parts.words: Gritty associate of Chopin, by George!
parts.note: something gritty that also names the novelist George, the lover of the composer Chopin

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a tough friend of the composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by George!' looks like an exclamation, but it gives the novelist's first name; George Sand was Chopin's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand is gritty material, and George Sand was the French novelist who lived with Chopin.

clue.text: Moroccan of Argentine extraction

indicators.note: extraction suggests something taken out and reshaped, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A North African with South American ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word; 'extraction' looks like ancestry but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Tangier, the Moroccan port, has this as a demonym.

clue.text: Flower girl on the fiddle

definitions.meaning: a female first name, as in Twelfth Night
a stringed instrument, larger than a violin

explanation.surface: A flower girl who plays the fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the' are link words. 'Flower girl' looks like one phrase, but it splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola names a pansy-like plant, a Shakespearean heroine and a stringed instrument like a big violin.

clue.text: Backward pull

parts.note: a pull towards yourself, as when hauling something or ... back a bowstring

explanation.surface: A tug in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something towards you is to haul it in, as a bowstring is hauled back.

clue.text: Dashed like Anglo-Saxons

definitions.meaning: joined with a short dash between parts
the compound is written with a dash joining its parts

explanation.surface: Early English people moving in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashed' suggests rushing, but it means written with a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A word joined with hyphens is written with dashes, as the compound Anglo-Saxon is.
